Compostella Valley Dear SB Members Trinidad and Secuya: 122 s. 2010 This pertains to your letter-query seeking our legal opinion on the following issues, to wit: "I. Is our practice in adopting the report correct and proper? 2. Is there an existing law that mandates local sanggunian to follow what is being written in the book by known authors? 3. Or thus the sanggunian itself has its autonomy to formulate its own Internal Rules of Procedures particularly in the adoption of the Committee report?" In reply thereto, please be informed that we already answered queries similar to those you raised above in DILG Opinion No. 76, s. 2007, dated 30 July 2009. In the said Opinion, we opined that Sanggunians are empowered to adopt their respective Internal Rules of Procedure, subject to the mandatory requirements provided under Section 50 of the Local Government Code (RA 7160) and provided further that it must be consistent with the Constitution and other pertinent laws. For your ready reference, please find the enclosed copy of the Opinion. Thank you and warm regards. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: . JES Director III LS:2 La B. DO UE IV

Different views then cropped up. For instance, that the Vice Governor as Presiding Officer is allowed to hold a regular committee because there is no such prohibition under the Local Government Code. Hence, your query. In reply thereto, please be informed that your query can be answered from the provisions of your Adopted IRI'. Allow us then to show you how we came up with SUCIi conclusion. When we say "arranged in the order of hierarchy", we mean that the higher source shall take precedence over the lower source. In other words, the lower source can only be applied in the absence of the higher source. May we now examine the 1987 Constitution and see whether or not there are parliamentary procedures contained therein that applies to Sanggunians. Unfortunately, while there are parliamentary rules contained in the Constitution, the same, however, apply only to Congress. The next source would be the Local Covernment Code and the sources of Parliamentary Rules of procedure can be found from Sections 48 to 59. Section 49 of the same Code speaks of the powers and limitations of the Presiding Officer. On the other hand, Section 50 speaks of the manner by which committee membership and chairmanship are to be determined. May we emphasize that Sections 49 and 50 do not contain any prohibition or allowance on the Presiding Officer to hold or chair a regular committee. There is iii fact nothing also there that expressly allowed the Presiding Officer to hold a special committee. In short, Sections 49 and 50 are silent on the malter. Because of Ellis silence of the Local Government Code, we have to go down to the next lower source, which is "Judicial Decisions". Judicial Decisions would refer to Supreme Court doctrines or parliamentary rules and procedures. Uillliortunately, however, we have yet to see a Supreme Court decision thali deals on the issue at hand. Such being the case, we have to go down to the next lower source, which is the Adopted Internal Rules of Procedure. Chis regard, may we note that Sanggunians are expressly empowered, under Section 50 of the Local Qovemment Code, to adopt its own Internal Kules of Procedure (IRI'). Such power, however, does not carry with it the power IAO alter or modify or disregard the provisions of law. Consequently, the the Sanggunian can only provide for matters that are not yet governed by Local Government Code source, particularly Sections 48 to 59 of the Local Government Code and other applicable laws. Hence, since as earlier stated, Sections 49 and 50 are silent as to whether or not the Vice Governor as Presiding Officer can hohl or chair a regular committee, this matter can be properly dealt with in the Adopted IRP of the Sanggunian. Therefore, if the Adopted IKP expressly prohibits the Vice Governor as presiding Officer to hold a regular committee, Chen said provision of the 1K? shall prevail.
